title: Guards Audit
eyebrow: Audit for approval · GitHub issue 285, "Guards block only unrecoverable actions" · nothing changed yet

short.lead: I went through every hook in hook.py (a hook is an automatic check) that can stop me. My test was yours: only data loss with no way back, or a change to someone else's work, should stop me. Nine kinds of destructive action are refused outright, and each refusal names the safe way to do the job instead. Deletes are refused only when the data isn't saved. You are asked only when no safe way exists and I cite a source proving it. Five workflow checks keep refusing, and each refusal now gives the exact fix, so I can correct course without stalling. The background-work guard is removed entirely. A page built by make_page.py is never refused again.
short.hint: Tap a card for what it guards today and what changes.
key: Refused, with the safe way named
items: Three things no guard may ever stop

You set these three requirements at 14:45 on 15 October. First, a routine commit or push to an agent-created branch other than main is never blocked. That means a branch named AjsAgent/, or a helper's own working-copy branch. Second, publishing a page built by make_page.py is never blocked. Third, I, or a helper I start, can always change files I created myself, inside the folder I was given. No prompt, refusal or timeout applies to any of them.
Nothing from you. It will be built first and tested by verify.py.
Nine kinds of destructive action, refused outright

1. Pushing or committing to main (the shared primary branch): open a pull request instead. 2. Commits, merges, rebases, cherry-picks and reverts on a branch the guard can't confirm is mine: make a new AjsAgent/ branch and commit there. 3. A force-push (overwriting history on the server), or a push with --all or --mirror: push a new branch instead. 4. Deleting a branch, local (branch -D) or remote (push --delete): leave it for you to delete. 5. git clean (deletes untracked files): move them into a _to_delete/ folder. 6. filter-branch (rewrites all history): rewrite on a copy branch. 7. git reset, git checkout -- or git restore while uncommitted work (changes not yet saved in git) exists: commit it on a new branch first. 8. stash drop or clear (discarding set-aside work): keep the stash. 9. Truncating (emptying) a file: write a new file beside it.
Nothing from you. You are asked only when no safe way exists and I cite a source proving it, such as the git manual.
Deletes are refused only when the file isn't saved

Today every delete command (rm) asks you first, even for a committed file git can restore. After this, a delete is refused in two cases. One is a recursive delete, which removes a whole folder (rm -r, rmdir /s, Remove-Item -Recurse). The other is a delete of a file that has uncommitted changes or was never committed. The refusal says to move the files into a _to_delete/ folder instead. Deleting a committed, unchanged file goes through, because git can bring it back.
Background work and process kills stop asking

These stop asking: background or hidden commands (nohup, a trailing &, Start-Process, background jobs), cutting a wait's output short with tail or head, and killing a process. None of these changes a branch or deletes saved work. The "Never hide work" rule text goes too, along with its 5-minute stall-check reminder.
Five workflow checks keep refusing, with the fix named

These force the right way of working, so they refuse outright. Each refusal gives the exact fix, so I correct course myself instead of stalling. 1. A page not built by make_page.py: the refusal gives the make_page.py command. 2. A Claude credit line or a claude/ branch name on GitHub: credit "AJ's agent" and use an AjsAgent/ branch. 3. An issue without its sections: add the missing ones it names. 4. A third helper (a sub-agent) running at once, or a helper starting its own helper: wait for one to finish. 5. Overwriting a whole file: a file I created myself goes through, while anyone else's file is refused with "edit it in place".

Today one unanswered prompt (a question asking for your OK) makes every later prompt in the session get refused straight away. That chain of refusals blocked both page publishes and the commit of the automatic-pages page. After this, you are asked only in the rare case where no safe way exists and I have cited a source proving it. The timer applies only to those prompts, never to anything else, such as publishing a page. Each prompt waits on its own, and nothing is refused because an earlier prompt went unanswered.
The copied reply always opens the gate

Today the copy box holds only the page's short label and your picks, such as "Guards audit: 1B". The design gate (the check that holds code edits until you approve a build plan) needs "Build plan approved: " followed by the plan's name, so the copied text never counts and I have to rebuild the page. After this, the copy box always holds the exact approval phrase plus your picks, and the page builder refuses to build a page whose copied text the gate wouldn't accept. Child issue 286: "Page copy box must hold the full reply the design gate accepts".
Credit and branch names come from each user, not from AJ

The plugin now has more users than you, so "AJ's agent" and AjsAgent/ can't be the same for everyone. Wherever this page says "AJ's agent" or AjsAgent/, read the name of each user's agent. The agent name defaults to the user's git name (the git config user.name setting). With no git name, it uses the part of their Claude account email before the "@", because the Claude account file stores no display name. The setting HOUSE_​RULES_​AGENT_​NAME replaces that default. Your git name is Ayden Wilkins, so your setup sets it to AJ to keep "AJ's agent" and AjsAgent/. Child issue 287: "Agent name, credit and branch prefix are configurable, not hard-coded to AJ".
Cards never cut text off on a phone

On your phone, the "Your name" card cut its text off mid-word. The card's two columns can't shrink below their longest word, and the page check only tests whether the whole page scrolls sideways. After this, card columns shrink and long words wrap. The check also opens every card and refuses the build if any text is cut off. Child issue 288: "Page cards clip long words on a phone, and the visual check misses it".

The design-loop lock stops code edits until you approve a build plan. You chose to keep it blocking (15 October, 15:04). So every plan reaches you as a page first, even though the helpers that write the code must wait while you're away.
Nothing more; your pick is recorded.
